subject: calendar
title: Angular Calendar and DatePicker have no isDateDisabled
description: React, Vue and vanilla accept an isDateDisabled predicate for both components; the Angular components declare no such input, so application-specific unavailable days (weekends, holidays) cannot be disabled in Angular. The guide's Calendar API table lists isDateDisabled without saying one adapter lacks it.

isDateDisabled?: (value: string) => boolean; onValueChange?: (value: string) => void;
['locale / weekStartsOn / isDateDisabled', 'string / 0–6 / predicate', 'Labels, week order, and application unavailability rules.']

Neither HwCalendarComponent (inputs at line 186) nor HwDatePickerComponent (line 238) declares isDateDisabled or any equivalent; React (calendar.tsx:20 "isDateDisabled?: (value: string) => boolean"), Vue (calendar.ts:55) and vanilla (calendar.ts:19 for Calendar, :149 for DatePicker) have it. subject: file-dropzone
title: Vanilla dropzone does not cancel dragover while disabled or read-only, so a blocked drop keeps the browser default
description: EXPANSION.md requires a blocked drop to prevent the drop's browser default. Vanilla only calls preventDefault on dragover when the input is enabled; without a cancelled dragover the browser never delivers drop to the zone and performs its default for dropped files (Chromium opens the file in the tab, leaving the form). The drop handler's preventDefault is therefore unreachable in the disabled case. React, Vue and Angular cancel dragover in the same state. docs/validation.md states that vanilla "already used effective disabled checks and is unchanged".

A blocked drop must

  and prevent the drop's browser default.

Vanilla already used effective
disabled checks and is unchanged.

subject: file-dropzone
title: Read-only differs: React has none, Angular renders it as disabled, Vue keeps a focusable aria-readonly input
description: React FileDropzoneProps omits readOnly. Angular readOnly binds [disabled]="disabled || readOnly", so the input leaves the tab order and form submission and gets the disabled style (axe also flags the instruction text contrast on the disabled background). Vue readonly keeps the input enabled and focusable, prevents the chooser and exposes aria-readonly; vanilla uses data-hw-readonly/aria-readonly on the root and prevents the chooser.

subject: container
title: Angular layout components drop host attributes, so documented data-variant/data-fit/data-tone and aria-label never reach the styled element
description: Every Angular layout component except Spacer renders the hw-* class on an internal element inside the <hw-*> host and does not forward host attributes. The documented CSS variants are selected by attributes on the hw-* element, so in Angular <hw-container data-variant="fluid">, <hw-aspect-ratio data-fit="contain"> and <hw-section data-tone="muted"> have no effect, and a native aria-label (or id) stays on the generic custom element. React and Vue forward these attributes to the hw-* element. Affects container (fluid), aspect-ratio (contain), section (tone, aria-label) and, for id/aria-*, every Angular primitive.

evidence.quote: Use `data-variant="fluid"` for a Container without the default outer gutters.

expected: Same variants and native attributes available in all adapters (docs/layout.md:233-235 states the variants without adapter restriction; React/Vue forward attributes, expanded-layout.tsx:10, layout.ts:35).
fix: Either render the hw-* class on the Angular host (host: {class, [style]} as HwSpacerComponent already does at layouts.ts:35) so host attributes apply, or add explicit inputs (variant, fit, tone, ariaLabel/id) and document that host attributes are not forwarded.

subject: stack
title: Polymorphic element (as) exists only in Vue; React renders an invalid as="..." attribute and Angular has no equivalent
description: Vue layout primitives accept as (default div, section for Section). React nativeLayout fixes the tag (div, or section for Section) and passes an unknown as prop straight to the DOM; Angular templates hard-code the element. A consumer can render <Stack as="nav"> or <Grid as="ul"> only in Vue. Applies to container, stack, inline, grid, columns, sidebar, center, spacer, aspect-ratio, section and app-shell.

evidence.quote: return function Layout({ gap, padding, align, justify, wrap, columns, minItemWidth, side, sidebarWidth, collapseAt, maxWidth, ratio, style, className, ...props }
Choose the appropriate semantic tag when an adapter offers `as`.

fix: Add a typed as prop to React nativeLayout (and strip it from DOM props); for Angular document attribute-selector usage or provide a tag input. Keep Section default section.

subject: page-header
title: PageHeader heading level is configurable only in Vue; React and Angular always render h1
description: Vue PageHeader has level (1-6). React and Angular hard-code <h1>, so PageHeader cannot be used for an embedded or secondary page section without creating a second h1. The guide itself recommends a lower heading in embedded compositions "when the adapter supports it". Also: React title is ReactNode, Vue title is String only.

evidence.quote: Use a lower heading in an embedded composition when the adapter supports it or use vanilla markup.

expected: Same heading-level control in all adapters (Vue layout.ts:96).
fix: Add level (React prop, Angular input) with the same 1..6 clamp; consider allowing rich title content in Vue via a title slot.

Ran /audit/verify/layout/p1-check.cjs with level 2. Script printed heading tag React H1, Vue H2, Angular H1 (ARIA: heading "T" [level=1] in React and Angular, [level=2] in Vue).
